text: 44-year-old female. The patient presents to the emergency department with confusion that started this morning. The patient's husband reports that she initially complained of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and fatigue after eating and has vomited 3 times. The patient has progressively become more confused throughout the day. The patient's past medical history includes morbid obesity, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, a sleeve gastrectomy 1 month ago, and depression with multiple suicide attempts.

speaker: Doctor

text: The normal CBC, lactate, and urinalysis effectively rule out sepsis and urinary infection, while the persistent severe hypoglycemia remains the primary driver of her confusion. Given the recent sleeve gastrectomy and diabetes history, I must rule out factitious hypoglycemia from insulin or sulfonylurea use; REQUEST TEST: Serum C-Peptide Level, REQUEST TEST: Insulin Level, REQUEST TEST: Oral Hypoglycemic Agent Screen.

text: RESULTS: Serum C-Peptide Level: Normal. Insulin Level: NORMAL READINGS. Oral Hypoglycemic Agent Screen: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal C-peptide and insulin levels rule out endogenous hyperinsulinism, while the negative sulfonylurea screen excludes oral hypoglycemic agents. Given the recent sleeve gastrectomy, the severe hypoglycemia is most consistent with post-bariatric late dumping syndrome due to exaggerated incretin response.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-bariatric late dumping syndrome
